articles.title: Nvidia pauses server shipments to Southeast Asia
articles.summary: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. This pause follows tighter United States regulations aimed at preventing advanced artificial intelligence chips from reaching markets in China.

articles.title: Social network X introduces parental controls
articles.summary: Elon Musk's platform X has finally added parental controls for teenagers after two decades. The feature allows parents and guardians to manage and monitor what content young users are able to see on the social media platform.

articles.title: S&P considers credit downgrade for Nvidia over governance
articles.summary: Credit rating agency S&P is considering lowering Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, which would be the fourth-highest rating, due to emerging concerns regarding corporate governance and associated key man risks.

articles.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan for space data centers
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to place artificial intelligence data centers in space. The agency dismissed opposition concerns regarding potential threats to scientific research, stating those issues fall outside its regulatory authority.

articles.title: OpenAI combines Chat and Work experiences
articles.summary: OpenAI is merging its Chat and Work experiences into a single system, introducing a unified usage meter. As a result, heavy users of ChatGPT may encounter usage limits much sooner than before under the combined structure.

articles.title: Tesla Cyrebruck becomes fast-selling used truck
articles.summary: The Tesla Cybertruck has emerged as the fastest-selling used truck in America, averaging just 39.1 days on the market. This significantly outperforms the overall truck market average of 65.5 days, despite earlier cancellations.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO defends human control in AI
articles.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed back against rivals' accusations that he supports surrendering human agency to artificial intelligence, even as leading tech companies increasingly automate their own research and model development processes.

articles.title: 1Password reports internal security breach
articles.summary: Password manager developer 1Password revealed that a hacker gained unauthorized access to an employee's corporate account and extracted certain customer information. However, the company assured users that all customer master passwords remain entirely safe.

articles.title: BYD unveils electric minivan with massive range
articles.summary: Chinese automaker BYD has announced a flagship electric minivan boasting an estimated range of 559 miles on a single charge. The vehicle offers expansive space for passengers, gear, and exceptionally large batteries for long-distance utility.

articles.title: Intel pressured to surrender stake for grants
articles.summary: Chipmaker Intel faced intense pressure to surrender a ten percent equity stake in order to unlock billions of dollars in previously promised government grants, or else face severe consequences.

articles.title: Peatland drainage contributes to global warming
articles.summary: A detailed historical estimate dating back to 1800 reveals that the continuous draining of peatlands around the world is directly responsible for a few percentage points of total global warming through carbon emissions.

articles.title: European spacecraft reveals chaotic asteroid aftermath
articles.summary: A European spacecraft observing the aftermath of an asteroid deflection experiment found a surprisingly chaotic scene. Researchers noted that the DART impact created a massive mess, though the exact nature remained previously unknown.

articles.title: Search alternative Kagi launches privacy email
articles.summary: Google search alternative Kagi has officially launched its own email service to rival Gmail. The new product features an unusual combination of strong privacy guarantees and integrated artificial intelligence capabilities.

articles.title: Backblaze clarifies customer data sharing policies
articles.summary: Cloud storage provider Backblaze addressed customer concerns by explaining its data sharing with advertisers. The company explicitly confirmed to reporters that it never shares users' private backup or storage files with third-party advertisers.

articles.title: FCC authorizes massive SpaceX satellite constellation
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy one million satellites into orbit. This massive proposed constellation would increase the total number of active satellites currently in orbit by roughly fifty times.

articles.title: Ladybird independent browser releases first alpha
articles.summary: The independent Ladybird browser engine has launched its first downloadable alpha version for Linux and macOS. Early testers found the new, scratch-built browsing software to be surprisingly capable during initial trials.

articles.title: Los Angeles school district blocks Google AI search
articles.summary: The Los Angeles school district has blocked Google's artificial intelligence search features on its networks. This action comes after the company insisted that its AI-generated overviews and core search functions are a permanent package deal.
